Continuing a Joint Score-Driven Filter Past the Series

Source: R/gas_joint_continue.R
term_continue.GasJoint.Rd

Computes the levels that the joint recursion reaches at rows that come after the observed ones.

Arguments

term

A built GasJoint().

psi

The parameters, as for term_filter().

f_past

The levels at the observed rows, a matrix with one column per filtered parameter.

s_past

The driving scores at the observed rows, a matrix like f_past.

newdata

The rows onto which to continue.

...

Ignored.

deriv

NULL, or a list with df_past and ds_past, lists with one matrix per filtered parameter (one row per observed row, m columns), and dpsi, the derivative of the joint parameter vector, one row per entry of term_params() and m columns.

Value

A matrix of continued levels with one row per row of newdata and one column per filtered parameter. With deriv, it carries the attribute "jacobian", a list with one nrow(newdata) by m matrix per filtered parameter.

Details

Past the data each driving score is at its conditional mean, zero, so the continuation is the deterministic recursion of each level, $$f_{k,n+h} = \omega_k + \sum_i \Big(\kappa_{k,i}\, u_{k,n+h-i} + \sum_{l \in C_k} \kappa_{k,i,l}\, u_{l,n+h-i}\Big) + \sum_j \xi_{k,j} f_{k,n+h-j},$$ in which the loadings contribute only while \(n+h-i\) is an observed time. A cross loading therefore reads the last observed scores of the other parameters of its group in the first steps, after which the levels evolve each on its own. The rules on the new rows are those of term_continue() for one term: each group continues its own series, the rows of a group are taken in time order and must come after every observed time of that group, and the terms must have been built with time.

See also

term_continue(), term_filter()
